Indications: Four months of intermittent solid-food dysphagia and post-meal epigastric discomfort; three months of
intermittent bright-red blood per rectum and a change in bowel habits. No hematemesis, melena, unintentional weight loss
or persistent vomiting. These examinations were ordered to evaluate active symptoms.
Preparation: The history and examination were reviewed, informed consent was obtained, and a procedural time-out was
completed. Stable hypertension is part of the medical history; no separate hypertension management was provided today.
No antiplatelet or anticoagulant use. No known drug allergies. ASA class II.
Sedation: Monitored anesthesia care was administered by a separate anesthesia team. Its medications, time and billing
are documented in a separate record, not in this report.
UPPER ENDOSCOPY - PERFORMED TODAY
The upper endoscope was introduced through the mouth and advanced to the second portion of the duodenum. The
examination was completed without limitation, with adequate visualization and no immediate complication.
Esophagus: Normal caliber and mucosa. No obstructing lesion, stricture, varices or visible Barrett-type change. Biopsies
were obtained with cold forceps from the proximal and distal esophagus for histologic evaluation (specimen B).
Esophageal dilation was considered before the procedure but was not performed because no narrowing was identified.
Stomach: Mild patchy antral erythema without ulceration or active bleeding. Cold-forceps biopsies were obtained from the
gastric antrum and body for histology and Helicobacter pylori testing (specimen A). Retroflexion showed no additional
lesion.
Duodenum: Bulb and second portion appeared normal. No duodenal biopsy or therapy was performed. No endoscopic
ultrasound or biliary procedure was performed during this examination.
Completion: Specimens A and B were retrieved. Estimated blood loss was minimal. Histology is pending.

COLONOSCOPY - PERFORMED TODAY
After digital rectal examination, the colonoscope was advanced to the cecum. The appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve
were identified and photographed. The terminal ileum was entered for approximately 5 cm and appeared normal; no ileal
biopsy was taken.
Extent
Complete to cecum and terminal ileum
Preparation quality
BBPS: right 2, transverse 3, left 3; total 8/9
Inspection
Withdrawal inspection: 14 minutes, excluding treatment
Limitations / complications
None; no immediate complication
LESIONS AND INTERVENTIONS
COL-1 - ascending colon: A 2 mm sessile polyp was completely removed in one bite with jumbo cold biopsy forceps and
retrieved as specimen C. Snare capture was technically difficult because of its position behind a fold. No snare resection
was performed on COL-1.
COL-2 - sigmoid colon: An 8 mm sessile polyp was removed en bloc by cold snare and retrieved as specimen D. Resection
was complete. No biopsy forceps were used on COL-2.
Resection-site care: One prophylactic clip was placed at the COL-2 resection site. There was no active bleeding and no
separate bleeding lesion was treated. Neither lesion required a lifting injection, cautery or ablation.
Lesion
Location / size
Technique actually performed
Specimen

COL-1 and COL-2 are different lesions at separate colonic sites. The forceps removal was not a biopsy of, or a completion
step for, the snare-treated sigmoid lesion. Both specimens were placed in separate labelled containers.
Other findings: Non-bleeding grade I internal hemorrhoids were seen on rectal retroflexion. The remaining colon appeared
normal. No additional lesion was sampled or treated. No colonic stricture, mass or active colitis was seen.
Completion: Both polyps were completely removed and retrieved. Estimated blood loss was minimal. The patient tolerated
the procedure and was transferred to recovery in stable condition.

POST-PROCEDURE ASSESSMENT
1. Intermittent solid-food dysphagia without a visible obstructing cause on today's examination; esophageal biopsies
pending.
2. Mild antral erythema; gastric biopsies pending. H. pylori infection, atrophic gastritis and intestinal metaplasia are not
established today.
3. Two distinct colonic polyps, completely removed by different techniques. Adenoma, dysplasia and malignancy cannot be
assigned from appearance alone; histology is pending.
4. Non-bleeding grade I internal hemorrhoids. The source of the intermittent hematochezia has not been definitively
established.
HISTORICAL AND PLANNED CARE - NOT SERVICES PERFORMED TODAY
Historical: An outside upper endoscopy dated 2024-06-12 reportedly showed mild gastric erythema. That examination was
a prior service, not a second upper endoscopy on 2026-11-03.
Planned: An EUS appointment for a pancreatic cyst seen on an outside MRI was arranged before this encounter for
2026-11-17. No EUS, cyst aspiration or ERCP was performed today. No separate cyst-management visit occurred today.
FOLLOW-UP AND AUTHENTICATION
Discharge after standard recovery criteria are met. Review pathology with the gastroenterologist in approximately two
weeks. The surveillance interval will be determined after histology. The patient received routine post-endoscopy
precautions. No separate office evaluation and management encounter or office-visit time is documented on this date.
